blocking.title: The credential check is still in the prompt check for google-vertex: RPC now refuses Vertex prompts that main sent
blocking.detail: turn_refusal(model) returns None only if is_runnable(model). For google-vertex, is_runnable calls _vertex_config_missing, and that function's own docstring calls it a GCP-auth check. It looks only at the environment: GOOGLE_CLOUD_API_KEY, or project and location. Two cases change over RPC, the one mode where main had no gate for this. (a) A keyless Vertex prompt. Main accepted and wrote it, then the adapter failed at request time with 'Vertex AI requires a project ID'. The tree refuses it before writing. (b) A Vertex key that comes from --api-key, auth.json or a models.json apiKey, with no GOOGLE_CLOUD_* env set. The adapter uses opts.api_key, and main sent the request. The tree refuses it with 'needs Google Cloud configuration before it can run'. Both contradict owner decision 1 (no new credential refusal in any mode; keyless behaves exactly as on main). They also contradict the CHANGELOG, guide and ADR-0239 d6 claims that only 'no model or no adapter' is refused and that 'a prompt whose provider has no key is handled exactly as before'. The TUI's #189 gate and the -p #98 gate already refused these on main, so only RPC changed. Fix: leave the Vertex auth arm out of turn_refusal, judging only provider, adapter and base URL, so the adapter's own error surfaces at request time as on main. Add RPC rows for keyless Vertex and for --api-key and auth.json keys. Alternatively, record it as an owner-approved exception and correct the docs.
